bank_change.title: Bank or payment detail change
bank_change.summary: Someone asks to send money to new banking or Interac details. This matches RCMP Scheme #2 style supplier payment redirection. Treat every change as suspicious until you speak with accounts payable using the number already on file.
redFlagPatterns: New transit, institution, or account numbers in email
Interac e-Transfer details that differ from what finance has on file
Sender domain close to a known supplier name but not exact
Urgent tone or a request not to call the usual contact
Attachment labeled void cheque or updated banking letter
oobSteps: Stop. Do not change anything in your payment system.
Find the supplier or customer phone number in your own directory or last paid invoice—not in this message.
Call that number and ask for accounts payable or the manager who handles banking.
Read back only the digits you already have on file and ask whether any change was requested.
If they confirm a change, have them send updated details through your normal secure channel and require a second manager sign-off before saving.
doNot: Do not trust a phone number, link, or PDF inside the email
Do not reply to the message to confirm banking details
Do not mark an invoice paid to new details without dual control

destination_change.title: Destination, dock, or yard change
destination_change.summary: A load headed to or from a Mississauga or Peel cold store may be sent to a different dock, yard, or address. Criminals use this to grab high-value food and beverage freight.
redFlagPatterns: New address or dock door sent close to pickup or delivery time
Change comes from a free webmail address
Message says the regular dock is full or closed without a name you recognize
Driver or carrier was not told through dispatch on file
oobSteps: Do not tell the driver to divert yet.
Call the shipper or receiver using the number in your TMS or partner list—not in the email.
Confirm dock, yard gate, and appointment with whoever runs receiving.
If the change is real, update the load in your system and notify the driver by your normal dispatch line.
Have a second person review high-value or temperature-controlled loads before release.
doNot: Do not release cargo to an unknown yard based on email alone
Do not share seal numbers with someone who only emailed
Do not skip calling because the message sounds urgent

credential_request.title: Portal, link, or access request
credential_request.summary: The message asks you to open a link, share a code, or reset access. Legitimate IT or partner access is arranged through known channels, not surprise email.
redFlagPatterns: Sign-in link that does not match your usual portal address
Request to forward a one-time code
Sender not on your approved domain list
Pressure to act before a shipment cutoff
oobSteps: Do not click links or open attachments from this message.
Call your IT help desk or the partner manager using the number already on file.
Ask whether they sent any access request today.
If access is needed, create it through your normal identity process with a second approver when policy requires.
Log what you verified and who approved it.
doNot: Do not type credentials into a page linked from email
Do not share multi-factor codes with anyone who calls or writes in
Do not install remote tools from an unsolicited link

new_carrier.title: New carrier or coverage offer
new_carrier.summary: An unknown carrier or broker offers to cover a load, sometimes as a sister company. Double brokering is a known problem in Canadian trucking.
redFlagPatterns: Carrier name not in your approved list or insurance file
Rate far below market with no prior relationship
MC or CVOR numbers that do not match the company name
Message from a personal mailbox instead of dispatch
oobSteps: Do not assign the load until the carrier is verified.
Call your regular broker or the customer contact on file.
Check insurance, authority, and past loads in your own records.
If you must use a new carrier, complete your onboarding checklist and get dual approval.
Tell the driver only after dispatch confirms in your system.
doNot: Do not book from a reply address you have never seen
Do not skip insurance verification because the load is hot
Do not pay a new factoring company without finance review

ot_remote.title: Plant or warehouse remote access
ot_remote.summary: Someone wants remote access to refrigeration controls, PLCs, or office systems tied to the cold store. OT changes can affect product safety and security.
redFlagPatterns: Vendor name you do not recognize for controls or refrigeration
Request to install remote support software quickly
After-hours urgency without a ticket number you can verify
Mix of IT and plant floor access in one email
oobSteps: Do not install software or open firewall rules from this message.
Call the vendor or internal maintenance lead using the number on your asset list or last work order.
Ask for a ticket or change number and match it to your system.
If access is approved, schedule it with maintenance present and log the session.
Review logs after the session ends.
doNot: Do not share VPN or jump box details by email
Do not let a caller bypass your change-control process
Do not assume a logo in the signature proves identity

first_order_credit.title: First order on credit terms
first_order_credit.summary: A new buyer wants product on credit before you have a payment history. Fraudsters mimic real distributors in the GTA food chain.
redFlagPatterns: Large first order with rush delivery
Credit application only by email
Trade references that go to mobile mailboxes
Billing address different from delivery cold store without explanation
oobSteps: Pause shipment until credit is approved through your normal process.
Call trade references using numbers you look up—not numbers in the application.
Confirm the business with your sales manager using contacts already on file.
Start with prepay or COD if policy allows until credit is established.
Document who approved any exception.
doNot: Do not ship high-value pallets on email promises alone
Do not skip credit checks because the brand name looks familiar
Do not send product to a one-time dock without verification

truck_status_update.title: Truck status or location update
truck_status_update.summary: A message claims a truck is loaded, delayed, or arrived. Use this to sync with dispatch, not as proof of identity or cargo release.
redFlagPatterns: Status change that does not match your GPS or TMS
Request to close the load or sign POD from email only
Unknown sender for a load you are tracking
oobSteps: Check your TMS or tracker first.
Call the driver or carrier dispatch on the number already on file.
Confirm location, seal, and temperature if the load is refrigerated.
Update your board only after verbal confirmation on your known line.
Keep the email as a record but do not treat it as authorization.
doNot: Do not release lumper or gate fees based on email alone
Do not change payment status because someone said delivered
Do not share the next load plan with an unverified contact

schedule_only.title: Appointment or schedule change only
schedule_only.summary: Pickup or delivery window changes at a cold store or DC. Lower risk than payment or diversion, but still verify through dispatch.
redFlagPatterns: Schedule change from a domain not on file
Last-minute change on a high-value lane
Conflicting times in the body and subject line
oobSteps: Compare the request to your existing appointment in the system.
Call receiving or the carrier on the number already on file.
Confirm date, time, dock door, and PO reference.
Update the slot in your scheduling tool after verbal OK.
Notify the driver through your normal channel.
doNot: Do not cancel a confirmed slot without speaking to the facility
Do not assume a calendar invite is from the real partner
Do not mix schedule changes with new payment instructions in one reply

bol_pod_alter.title: Bill of lading or POD change
bol_pod_alter.summary: Someone wants seal numbers, weights, or proof of delivery edited. This can hide theft or support false claims.
redFlagPatterns: Revised BOL attached after pickup
Request to backdate delivery
Seal number different from what the driver reported
POD without matching receiver name
oobSteps: Do not accept altered documents until verified.
Call the shipper and receiver using numbers on the original BOL or your directory.
Compare seal, piece count, and temperature readings with driver notes.
If a correction is legitimate, have the partner reissue through your document portal or fax on file.
Scan and attach the verified version to the load file.
doNot: Do not reprint POD to match a fraudulent claim
Do not share blank BOL templates by email
Do not sign for short or damaged goods without receiver confirmation on your known line
